# CONVENTIONS
Schema edition 2026-09-29 · kit edition 2026-09-29 · created 2026-09-29
Every convention, blueprint correction, examiner rule and schema change is dated here (P§21).

## 2026-09-29 · Batch 0
- **Auto-vault.** Artifact "PHY-042 VAULT" = https://claude.ai/artifact/B7cPAEtFTDXQKCxkXD8PZY (capabilities db + assets). Round-trip test PASS: db-export -> write_db (20 writes) -> read_db (meta 1 + vault 19) -> db-import into scratch -> 19/19 files byte-identical. vault_url stored in STATE.
- **Kit location.** The project copy is named `pyqkit_py.txt`; the CI§3 pattern `pyqkit*.py*` does not match it. Boot also looks for `pyqkit_py.txt` (logged in Q-QUEUE as a CI conflict).
- **Syllabus verified (PHY-05 vs Physics_SecP2_2026-27.pdf).** All 108 IN topics map to the Class XII theory text (pp. 13-16); every limitation note matches the printed wording; the 21 VERIFY-DEL and 1 DELETED topics are absent from the syllabus text. VERIFY-DEL is kept (the NCERT rationalised list is not in the project). Paraphrase noted, not an error: T-04-02 says "field on the axis of a circular loop"; the syllabus says "application to current carrying circular loop".
- **Unit marks (image p12):** I+II 16 · III+IV 17 · V+VI 18 · VII+VIII 12 · IX 7 · total 70. The Unit IX cell PRINTS 7 and its chapter line reads "Chapter-14". PHY-04 §1's "Chapter 7-14" and "blank Unit IX cell" are text-layer damage (the 7 slides out of its cell), not errors in the document. VERIFIED on image.
- **Thinking-level design (image p23):** Remember+Understand 27 (38 %) · Apply 22 (32 %) · Analyse+Evaluate+Create 21 (30 %); theory 70 + practical 30. The p23 note points to the "Sample Question Paper of class XII for the year 2026-27".
- **Syllabus intro** reads "Class XI-XII (2025-26)" at the top of p1 and "Class XI-XII (2026-27)" at its foot (text layer; p1 image not viewed).
- **Sample paper in the project is the 2025-26 SQP** (p1 image: "CLASS - XII (2025 - 26)"; footer: the 2024-25 scheme "will continue in the current session i.e. 2025-26"). It is the sample paper for the 2026 exam: paper_id SQP2526-042, exam SQP, year 2026. It is mined at Batch 0 and belongs to the 2026 year for the Definition of Done. PHY-04 §2's SQP 2026-27 details (VI alternative inside Q9; text damage 168O, "B and B", 300 for 30 deg) are absent from this file, so PHY-04 §2 describes a different document (the official 2026-27 SQP, not in the project).
- **SQP 2025-26 scoring lines.** No SQP scheme is in the project. Its steps are written in the Y2026 scheme pass: TRANSFERRED:<award_id> from printed 2026 board-scheme steps of the same archetype, otherwise INFERRED (labelled). Never mixed with PRINTED.
- **2027 blueprint.** Until an SQP 2026-27 BLUEPRINTS row exists, plan-mock uses the kit default P33 (choice at 20, 21, 27, 31-33), which is also what SQP 2025-26 prints (see its BLUEPRINTS row).
- **W-1 scheme-year check.** The rotating schemes XII-2-042-*.pdf are 2026 board schemes (55/1/1 image: "MARKING SCHEME: PHYSICS (042) Session: 2025-26 Code: 55/1/1"). They match the next year to mine (2026). Each file's identity is confirmed on its own image at Y2026 S1.
- **FILES status changes** go through ERRATA rows (Layer 1 is append-only); ids ER-B<nn>-<nnn>.
- **Part rows.** Printed sub-part labels ((I), (II), (A), (B), (a), (i) ...) become separate rows with the label as printed in `part`. Unlabelled linked demands ("... Hence define ...") stay one row unless they test different skeletons (then -d1/-d2). The kit counts one event per (paper, question, side, code), so parts sharing a code are never double-counted. The suffix -VI is reserved for visually-impaired alternatives.
- **FORMULAE role `asked`** holds the relation a printed demand requires (read from the demand on the page image, not from a scheme); `given` holds formulas printed in the stem.
- **VI alternatives in SQP 2025-26** sit inside Q5, Q6, Q7, Q18 and Q20(II) (so far); none of them is counted in marks.
- **Classification rule (P§10.2 applied, 2026-09-29).** A row takes an existing code only when its demand is that archetype's core demand and the archetype's scoring skeleton earns full marks on it with no new idea; a narrower or different demand (e.g. "write the expression" against "derive it") gets its own code in the same family. MCQ and A-R items get their own "(MCQ)" / "(A-R)" codes (P§10.3.5), including MCQ sub-parts of case studies. Labelled parts that share one skeleton share one code (one event).
- **VI alternatives** are classified only when an existing code fits cleanly; the rest stay unclassified. VI rows never enter statistics or the Definition of Done (kit rule), so this loses nothing.
- **Skeletons of codes issued from SQP 2025-26** come from the printed demand (no scheme in the project) and are refined from printed scheme lines when a scheme exercises the same code.

## 2026-09-29 (UTC) · Batch 1
- **2026 series (p1 images).** 55/1 QPSR1 · 55/2 R2SQP · 55/3 PQS3R (+ 55(B), set 5) · 55/4 RP4QS · 55/5 R5QPS · compartment 55/7 S7PQR (+ 55(B)/7, set 5).
- **Letter codes.** The VI papers print "55(B)" and "55(B)/7"; their scheme prints "Code: 55/ B". Written paper_code 55/B and 55/B/7, paper_id 2026-55B and 2026C-55B7, so paper and scheme share one code in COVERAGE.
- **Compartment.** Series 55/7 is recorded exam COMPT, tag 2026C, from ZIP identity (2,364,538 bytes = the official 2026-COMPTT Physics ZIP size in PHY-04 s4; entries dated 2026-07-29) and its separate series. The papers print no exam type.
- **Year evidence, 2026 papers.** No 2026 paper prints a year. Evidence: the same-code scheme printing "Session 2025-26" (image), the PDF creation year, and the official ZIP size; the content match with the scheme is confirmed per paper at S5.
- **Scheme bundles are image-only scans.** Text layer = a contents page on p1 and "HOME" link words elsewhere, so the dual-read is impossible: every scoring line is read from the 924-px JPEG, enlarged; a line still uncertain -> UNREADABLE LOWRES + one optional single-page request. Layout (55/1/1): p1 contents, p2-p3 the 18 examiner instructions + an OSM note on choice questions, p4 onward value points; 55/4/1 starts its value points on p3.
- **Origins.** Set 1 of each series is the S3 origin (all sets are clean originals); siblings and the two VI papers are S4 work of their series.
- **Bilingual originals.** Hindi and English pages alternate, and the kit's page table marks the Hindi pages "en" (their text layer is not Unicode), so English pages are picked per paper at S3 from the page text (55/1/1: odd pages 3-31).
- **Choice inside a case sub-part (2026 boards).** Q29 and Q30 carry an OR alternative inside one sub-part, printed after OR without its own label. Rows: the untouched sub-parts keep side blank (`-Q29-I`); the alternatives take sides A and B at question level with the sub-part label as printed context (`-Q29A-III`, `-Q29B-III`), one choice_pair_id `OR-<paper>-Q29`, and `extra` choice_in_part=III. check-paper counts the question once. BLUEPRINTS choice_rule lists such questions under D (e.g. `D:29,30`).
- **Sides printed as (a) OR (b).** A single-part alternative labelled (a)/(b) (e.g. 55/1/1 Q18) is written as sides A/B with no part; where each side has its own (a), (b) parts, those are the parts (`-Q22A-a`).
- **Printed sub-labels (i), (ii) inside a part** become their own rows (`-Q22A-b-i`), as the Batch 0 part-row rule says.
- **A shared case figure** gets one full FIGURES description on the first dependent row and short pointer rows on the other dependent rows, so every has_figure row has its figure.
- **Documents are opened by file_id**, not paper_id, while Q-008 is open.
- **Kit edition 2026-09-30 (B01).** Two tested fixes, shipped in tools/: (1) check-paper counts side-blank rows as common to both alternatives when a question also has sides A/B, so printed sub-part marks of a case with a choice inside one sub-part (55/2/1 Q29, Q30: 1 mark each) add up to the question total; (2) a paper_id shared by a paper and its scheme resolves to the question paper, and an exact file_id always wins (Q-008). Tests: 2026-5521, 2026-5511 and SQP2526-042 PASS; validate 16/16; a planted sub-part overflow is still caught. Previous edition kept as a local backup only.
- **Reading time** (all 20 papers): the cover note "(V) 15 minute time has been allotted to read this question paper" was checked on the 55/1/1 cover image; the other 19 covers carry the same note in their text layer.
- **S4 method (B01).** Sibling questions are matched to the origin by text similarity, then every sibling page is read on its image. A question with identical text and numbers becomes a shuffle row (a copy of the origin row with the sibling's own id, q_no, source_page, choice and case ids, rel = shuffle, rel_to = origin row); its printed figures and formulae are copied with the sibling's pages. A question that differs in any way is extracted fully as rel = origin, with a note naming the origin question it resembles. The ARSET goes on the sibling's own first assertion-reason row.

## 2026-10-01 (UTC) · Batch 2 · Claude Code route
- **Route.** Mining moved to Claude Code cloud sessions over three GitHub repositories found by content: instructions (read only), project (vault file and the year's schemes; the only repository committed to), papers (question-paper ZIPs; read only). The chat project audits read only while Claude Code mines; its findings arrive as `Fix:` lines (one writer at a time).
- **Checkpoint.** `phy_gate.py` merges part files, writes the status erratum and the PROGRESS line with counts computed from the tables, validates, packs into `outputs/vault/` of the project repository, commits and pushes after every paper. This replaces the auto-vault database and her manual vault swap. `STATE.json` gains the key `cc_session` (additive).
- **Double-read.** From Batch 2, every paper's marks, numbers, options and figure values are read twice: by an extractor and by a blind checker who sees only the row skeleton. The gate compares the two readings; every mismatch is settled from a 300-400 dpi crop and logged (`outputs/logs/GATE-LOG-B02.md`, `outputs/logs/doublecheck/`).
- **Originals.** Files the chat saw as 924-px bundles now come from GitHub as original PDFs with their own FILES rows; each takes its twin's identity through ERRATA (S1b). Scoring lines are read from the originals.
- **Kit edition 2026-09-30b** (made and tested in the chat on 2026-09-30, first used at Batch 2): a row may name its series in `extra` as `series=55/3`; V07 and `similar` use it. The letter-code visually-impaired papers carry it on every row: 2026-55B `series=55/3; vi_paper=y`, 2026C-55B7 `series=55/7; vi_paper=y`, so their unchanged questions are shuffles of their own series and are not counted twice. Tests: validate 16/16 on the Batch 1 vault; a 55B shuffle of a 2026-5531 row passes V07 only with the key; a 55B7 row with `series=55/7` pointing at a 55/3 row fails.
- **S1b result (B02).** 17 originals took their bundle twins' identity (16 2026 schemes and the syllabus; ER-B02-001..ER-B02-071), each confirmed on its own page images: p1 (scheme contents page with "PHYSICS (042) Code: ...", or the 55/4/1 instructions page) and, for the schemes, the first value-point header "MARKING SCHEME: PHYSICS (042) Session: 2025-26 Code: ...". Two new files are not twins: Physics-MS.pdf is the marking scheme of SQP 2025-26 (SQP-MS, SQP2526-042; ER-B02-072..ER-B02-076; Q-012); Physics-SQP (1).pdf is the 2024-25 sample paper (SQP2425-042, stays NEW for its year; ER-B02-077..ER-B02-078).
- **Syllabus p1 (correction to the Batch 0 line "Syllabus intro reads ...").** The original's p1 image prints only "Class XI-XII (2026-27)"; the "(2025-26)" read at the top of p1 in Batch 0 is a hidden object in the text layer, which the image does not show. PHY-04 §1's "intro still says 2025-26" is therefore text-layer damage too (Q-002).
- **Scheme repository (B02 layout).** The 2026 scheme PDFs sit in a repository that holds neither a vault file nor a ZIP, so `phy_code_env.py` gives it no role and links none of its files; the vault file sits in the instructions repository, which therefore also serves as the project repository (`outputs/` and the pushes go there). At B02 the 16 scheme PDFs were linked into /mnt/project by hand (links only, no repository changed) before inventory, which therefore recorded them where=project. Repeat the links at boot until the layout or the setup changes (Q-011).
- **Opening a document by file_id on this route:** `pyqkit pages` and `render` need `--vault /home/claude/vault` (the kit's default vault is empty); R§3's commands omit it (Q-011).
- **A shuffle whose origin row misreads the shared figure (B02).** The row stays rel = shuffle (the page images are identical); its own FIGURES and FORMULAE rows describe what the page shows and its note names the origin rows that disagree; the origin rows change only through ERRATA with crop evidence (a Fix), never by copying the error forward (2026-5532-Q19A; Q-013).

## S5 scheme pass (B02, first scheme 55/1/1)
- **Examiner instructions, 2026 board schemes (55/1/1 pp2-3, register R14):** marks strictly by the value points, but competency-based answers and correct answers from other expressions or newer knowledge get due marks (4, 5); an error is penalised once, never for its cumulative effect (10); full scale 0-70 used (11); a candidate who attempts both alternatives is marked on both and the higher counts (17); an unattempted alternative is marked NA (18); OSM marking, part marks on the right, unparted questions in the left margin (8, 9). No instruction on half marks or units: halves appear only in the value points. Later sets note only differences.
- **Key rows:** an MCQ or assertion-reason answer is one `key` row whose step_text is the printed letter only, e.g. `(C)`, marks 1; the option text it names is already on the paper row. An OR alternative key with no mark printed beside it takes the sub-part's 1.
- **Combined mark cells** ("½ + ½", "½ + ½ + ½" beside one line that lists several items) are one STEP-AWARDS row per printed half, the cell's text kept in each step_text; the blind checker lists them the same way.
- **Unmarked routes:** "Alternatively" methods and "award full marks for any other ..." notes carrying no marks of their own go into `alt_accepted` of the line they replace; they are not scoring lines. `mandatory = y` only where the scheme says a line is compulsory.
- **Scheme symbols** that differ from the paper's (55/1/1 Q24 uses L for the plate separation) are kept as printed in step_text; the mapping note in notes/Y2026.md says what they stand for.
- **A half mark printed between two parts' lines** goes where the scheme's own description box (the per-question split printed at the top of each answer) puts it (55/1/2 Q27: box (b) 1, (c) ½ + 1).

# Q-QUEUE (never blocking)

- [Q-001 · 2026-09-29 · open] The 2026-27 sample paper and its marking scheme are not in project knowledge; the project's Physics-SQP.pdf is the 2025-26 paper. Until they are added, the 2027 blueprint rests on the kit default (identical to what SQP 2025-26 prints) and on PHY-04 §2's earlier reading. Non-blocking.
- [Q-002 · 2026-09-29 · open] PHY-04 §1 correction for the next `Research update.`: the syllabus Unit IX cell prints 7 and the chapter line reads "Chapter-14" (p12 image). Remove the two "document errors" from PHY-04 §1. - [Q-003 · 2026-09-29 · open · CI conflict] CI§3 step 1's find pattern `pyqkit*.py*` misses the project copy `pyqkit_py.txt`. Worked around by also matching that name. Fix in CI§3 wording when the instructions are next edited.
- [Q-004 · 2026-09-29 · open] No marking scheme for SQP 2025-26 in the project: its scoring lines will be TRANSFERRED from 2026 printed steps (same archetype) or INFERRED.
- [Q-005 · 2026-09-29 · resolved B01: exam COMPT from ZIP identity (size = official 2026-COMPTT ZIP, entries dated 2026-07-29) and the separate series S7PQR; the papers print no exam type] The smaller ZIP (PHYSICS__10_.zip: 55/7/1-3 and 55(B)-7) was tagged MAIN by inventory from text alone; its size matches the official 2026 compartment ZIP (PHY-04 §4). Confirm exam type on page images at Y2026 S1 and correct with ERRATA.
- [Q-006 · 2026-09-29 · resolved B01: all 16 identities read from page images, ERRATA ER-B01] The 16 rotating scheme bundles have near-empty text layers, so inventory left kind UNKNOWN / year UNK / paper_id blank (and no code for XII-2-042-4-1). Correct each from its own page image at Y2026 S1 (ERRATA).
- [Q-007 · 2026-09-29 · open · kit] `status` lists the verified syllabus file under "fully mined" (it counts every DONE file); wording fix for the next kit edition, no data impact.

- [Q-008 · 2026-09-29 · resolved B01 by kit edition 2026-09-30: an exact file_id wins and a shared paper_id resolves to the question paper] `pages`/`render` resolve a paper_id to the first FILES row carrying it; once a scheme shares its paper's paper_id (as P5.2 intends), `render 2026-5511` opened the scheme bundle. PH-05-009,FAM-05-02 Magnetic materials,05,T-05-05,DGM,Draw field lines through diamagnetic and paramagnetic substances,Asks you to draw how uniform field lines bend away from a diamagnetic sample and crowd into a paramagnetic sample.,Diamagnetic: lines pushed out (fewer inside); paramagnetic: lines drawn in (more inside); labels,Drawing both alike or reversing them (SQP 2025-26 Q20(II)),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q20B-A,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-06-009,FAM-06-02 Lenz's law,06,T-06-03,MCQ,Compare a magnet's fall through a coil and through air (MCQ),Asks you to use Lenz's law to see that induced currents in a metal coil or tube oppose a falling magnet and slow it down.,"1 mark for the option; induced current opposes the change, so the fall takes longer","Answering the same time, or an infinite time (SQP 2025-26 Q9)",VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q09,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-07-012,FAM-07-02 Single-element AC circuits,07,T-07-02,MCQ,Identify an AC circuit element from its phasor diagram (MCQ),"Asks you to decide which element a phasor diagram shows from the phase between current and voltage, then predict how its reactance behaves.",1 mark for the option; current leads by 90 deg: capacitor; lags by 90 deg: inductor; in phase: resistor,Reading lead and lag the wrong way round (SQP 2025-26 Q3),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q03,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-07-013,FAM-07-05 AC devices,07,T-07-07,MCQ,Find a generator's emf when its rotation speed changes (MCQ),Asks you to see that changing an AC generator's angular speed changes both the frequency and the peak emf of its output.,1 mark for the option; e = N*B*A*omega*sin(omega*t): amplitude and frequency both scale with omega,Changing only the frequency and keeping the peak emf (SQP 2025-26 Q10),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q10,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-07-014,FAM-07-05 AC devices,07,T-07-07,NUM,Find the peak emf of a coil rotating in a magnetic field,"Asks you to find the field acting on a rotating coil, for example inside a solenoid, and then its maximum induced emf.",B = mu0*n*I (solenoid) or as given; e_max = N*B*A*omega; substitution; result with unit,Using the solenoid's turns for the coil's; area units; note: no angular speed printed in SQP 2025-26 Q28,VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q28,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-07-015,FAM-07-03 Series LCR and resonance,07,T-07-03,NUM,"Find impedance, current and power in a series LCR circuit","Asks you to use the resistance and the two reactances to find the circuit's impedance, then the current and the average power it takes.",Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2); I = V/Z (rms); P = I^2*R or V*I*cos(phi); results with units,Peak values used for power; X_L and X_C added instead of subtracted (SQP 2025-26 Q33(II)(A)),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q33B-A-ii,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-08-008,FAM-08-03 EM spectrum,08,T-08-04,MCQ,Compare frequency and photon energy across the EM spectrum (MCQ),"Asks you to compare two EM waves, such as radio waves and gamma rays, by frequency, wavelength or energy from their places in the spectrum.",1 mark for the option; order of the spectrum; E = h*nu,Confusing wavelength order with energy order (SQP 2025-26 Q4),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q04,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-08-009,FAM-08-02 EM wave properties,08,T-08-02,NUM,Write the electric field equation of a plane EM wave,"Asks you to write the electric field of a plane wave as an equation, finding its amplitude, wave number and direction from the given magnetic field.",E0 = c*B0; k = omega/c; direction from E x B along the travel; E = E0*sin(k*x - omega*t) with its unit vector,Wrong direction of E; nT not converted to T (SQP 2025-26 Q17),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q17,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-09-015,FAM-09-02 Refraction and total internal reflection,09,T-09-03,MCQ,Trace a ray through a right-angled prism using the critical angle (MCQ),"Asks you to choose the correct path of light through a right-angled isosceles prism, deciding where total internal reflection happens from the critical angle.",1 mark for the option; angle of incidence at each face against the critical angle; TIR where it is reached,Letting light refract out where it meets the critical angle (SQP 2025-26 Q5),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q05,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-09-016,FAM-09-02 Refraction and total internal reflection,09,T-09-03,AR,Judge statements on critical angle and the colour of light (A-R),"Asks you to decide whether statements about how the critical angle depends on colour and wavelength are true, and whether the reason explains the assertion.","sin(C) = 1/n; n is larger for violet, so C is smallest for violet; test R's wavelength claim; choose the option",Accepting the false claim about wavelength order (SQP 2025-26 Q14),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q14,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-09-017,FAM-09-03 Lenses,09,T-09-06,NUM,Use the lens maker's formula to find focal length or radius,Asks you to apply the lens maker's formula with correct signs to find a lens's focal length or the radius of curvature it needs.,1/f = (n - 1)*(1/R1 - 1/R2); sign convention (R2 = -R for equi-convex); substitution; result with unit,Sign of R2 for an equi-convex lens (SQP 2025-26 Q32(I)(B)),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q32A-B,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-10-009,FAM-10-03 Diffraction,10,T-10-05,MCQ,Predict how the single-slit pattern changes with slit width (MCQ),"Asks you to pick the intensity graph for a single slit after its width changes, knowing the central maximum narrows as the slit widens.","1 mark for the option; central width = 2*lambda*D/a; wider slit: narrower central maximum, more light through",Choosing a wider pattern for a wider slit (SQP 2025-26 Q6),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q06,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-10-010,FAM-10-02 Interference,10,T-10-03,AR,Judge statements on coherent sources (A-R),"Asks you to decide whether statements about what makes two light sources coherent are true, and whether the reason explains the assertion.",Coherent means a constant phase difference; similar wavelength alone is not enough; choose the option,Treating similar wavelength as coherence (SQP 2025-26 Q15),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q15,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-11-008,FAM-11-02 Matter waves,11,T-11-05,GRF,Plot de Broglie wavelength against inverse root of voltage and find slope,Asks you to draw the straight-line graph of de Broglie wavelength against one over the square root of the accelerating voltage and find its slope.,lambda = h/sqrt(2*m*q*V); straight line through the origin; slope = h/sqrt(2*m*q); labelled axes,Drawing a curve; slope missing the charge (SQP 2025-26 Q21(II)),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q21B,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-11-009,FAM-11-01 Photoelectric effect,11,T-11-04,PRD,Predict how photocurrent changes with collector potential or supply,"Asks you to say how the photocurrent reading changes when the collector's potential is made less positive or negative, or the supply voltage is changed.",Accelerating potential: current rises to saturation; retarding potential: falls to zero at the stopping potential; reason,"Saying the current drops as soon as the potential falls, even at saturation (SQP 2025-26 Q30(II))",VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q30-II,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-12-008,FAM-12-02 Bohr model and spectra,12,T-12-05,MCQ,Pick the hydrogen transition that emits the longest wavelength (MCQ),"Asks you to pick, from an energy-level diagram or list, the emission with the smallest energy gap and so the longest wavelength.",1 mark for the option; emission is a downward transition; lambda = h*c/delta_E; smallest gap gives the longest lambda,Choosing an upward (absorption) transition or the largest gap (SQP 2025-26 Q7),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q07,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-12-009,FAM-12-02 Bohr model and spectra,12,T-12-04,AR,Judge statements on the energy of a Bohr-orbit electron (A-R),Asks you to decide whether statements about the electron's negative total energy and the force keeping it in orbit are true and linked.,Total energy is negative because the electron is bound; the centripetal force is the electrostatic attraction; decide whether R explains A,Linking two true statements automatically (SQP 2025-26 Q13),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q13,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-12-010,FAM-12-01 Rutherford model,12,T-12-01,PRD,Relate impact parameter to how alpha particles are scattered,Asks you to say how the impact parameter changes the scattering angle of alpha particles and give its value for a head-on collision.,"Small impact parameter: large deflection; large: small deflection; head-on: b = 0, particle turns back at 180 deg",Reversing the relation (SQP 2025-26 Q21(I)),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q21A,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-13-008,FAM-13-01 Nuclear size and force,13,T-13-01,MCQ,Compare the densities of nuclei of different mass numbers (MCQ),Asks you to see that nuclear density is the same for all nuclei because the nuclear radius grows as the cube root of the mass number.,1 mark for the option; R = R0*A^(1/3); density independent of A,Taking the ratio of mass numbers or of radii (SQP 2025-26 Q11),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q11,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"
PH-14-009,FAM-14-03 p-n junction and diode,14,T-14-04,MCQ,Find current or voltage in a diode circuit with threshold drops (MCQ),"Asks you to decide which diodes conduct, subtract their threshold drops or add their forward resistances, and choose the resulting current or voltage.",1 mark for the option; bias check; Si 0.7 V and Ge 0.3 V drops or forward resistance; Ohm's law,Letting a reverse-biased diode conduct; forgetting a conducting diode's drop (SQP 2025-26 Q29),VERIFIED,,0,SQP2526-042-Q29-I,"issued at Batch 0 from SQP 2025-26; skeleton from the printed demand (no scheme in project), to be refined from printed scheme lines"

CS-SQP2526-042-Q29,SQP2526-042,29,"A passage on biasing a p-n junction diode: forward bias (p-side to the positive terminal) and reverse bias (n-side positive), with the applied voltage dropping mostly across the depletion region. CS-SQP2526-042-Q30,SQP2526-042,30,"A passage on the photoelectric effect in a photocell: light of suitable frequency ejects electrons from emitter C, which are drawn to collector A and give a microampere current that follows the illumination, useful in control and light-measuring devices. It quotes a work function of 6.35 eV for platinum, and the figure shows the tube fed through a sliding contact B on a row of cells with a microammeter.",11,3,"NUM,PRD,GRF","all three (no choice printed); marks printed per part 2, 1, 1",11,0

CS-2026-5521-Q29,2026-5521,29,"A passage on the p-n junction: doping makes p- or n-type material, majority carriers give the diffusion current and the barrier field drives minority carriers as the drift current, the two being equal in an unbiased diode. # PHY-03 addendum (entries added at Batch 0; the full file was delivered as PHY-03-MISTAKES-LEDGER.md)

### G · Batch 0 (29 September)
- **B0-1 · The project's sample paper was last session's.** `Physics-SQP.pdf` prints "CLASS – XII (2025 – 26)"; CBSE reuses that file name every year, and PHY-04 §2's "SQP 2026-27" details (VI alternative inside Q9; text damage 168O, "B and B", 300) are absent from it. Caught at boot from the page-1 image.
  → A permanent file's session is read from its page-1 image, never from its name; a mismatch is logged and the file is mined for what it is → CI§7, P§5
- **B0-2 · Two "errors in the official syllabus" in PHY-04 §1 were text-layer damage.** The page-12 image prints 7 marks for Unit IX and "Chapter–14"; the text layer had moved the 7 into the chapter line.
  → A claimed error in an official document is recorded only after its page image confirms it → CI§2, P§6
- **B0-3 · The boot search pattern `pyqkit*.py*` misses the project copy `pyqkit_py.txt`.** The kit was found by listing the folder.
  → Boot also matches `pyqkit_py.txt`; the CI wording is queued for correction → CI§3
- **B0-4 · The first Batch 0 reply stopped at the tool limit before its checkpoint,** leaving the database copy older than the disk for one turn (nothing lost; `Resume` packed first).
  → Checkpoint right after the gate items, before opening a paper, as well as after each paper → CI§6
- **B0-5 · Inventory reads identity from text only;** the 2026 scheme bundles have near-empty text layers, so kind, year and paper id came out unknown.
  → Image-only files get their identity from their page images at S1 intake, through ERRATA → P§5

### Part 3 addition
- **W-13 · A permanent file replaced by last session's twin** (CBSE reuses names such as `Physics-SQP.pdf` every year).
  → Boot compares each permanent file's printed session with the one the CI names; a mismatch is logged in one line and never blocks → CI§7

### H · Batch 1 (29-30 September)
- **B1-1 · The first Batch 1 reply hit the tool limit before its first checkpoint (a repeat of B0-4).** About thirty separate calls went to boot reads and identity crops; the identity confirmations lived only in the chat until the next turn. Nothing was lost (the vault was unchanged), but a repeat is the worst outcome this ledger names.
  → Boot reads are batched into one or two calls; each stage's findings are written to disk by one script as soon as they are read; the first checkpoint comes right after S1, before any paper page is opened -> CI s6, P s11
- **B1-2 · A paper_id opened the wrong document.** After S1 gave each scheme its paper's paper_id, `render 2026-5511` rendered the scheme bundle; caught at once from the text printout, before any row was written.
  → Documents are opened by file_id; kit fix queued (Q-008) -> P s4
- **B1-3 · The kit could not total a case study whose choice sits inside one sub-part when sub-part marks are printed** (55/2/1 Q29, Q30): it summed each side alone, so the paper failed check-paper though nothing was wrong on the page.
  → Fixed once in kit edition 2026-09-30 (common sub-parts count with each alternative), tested on every mined paper plus a planted overflow, logged, shipped in tools/ -> CI s7, P s4
- **B1-4 · A test script rewrote a scratch table without closing the file before the check ran,** so the check read a half-written file and reported missing questions. Scratch copy only; the vault was never touched.
  → Test harnesses close (or use `with`) every file before calling the kit -> P s4
- **B1-5 · A row count was typed into a PROGRESS line by hand (79 for 55/3/1) instead of taken from the data; the kit had just printed 72.** Caught before the checkpoint went out; corrected from the table.
  → Progress lines take their counts from the tables in the same script, never from memory -> CI s2.7
- **B1-6 · The time estimate in a reply said 13 sibling papers were left; the tables said 12.** The count was typed before the tables were read.
  → Counts in replies, estimates included, come from a script run earlier in the same turn -> CI s2.7

### Part 3 additions (Batch 2, Claude Code route)
- **W-14 · Two miners writing one vault** (the chat and Claude Code at once): restore keeps only the newest copy, so the other one's work vanishes silently.
  → One writer at a time: Claude Code mines; the chat audits read only and sends `Fix:` lines → CLAUDE.md §3, PHY-07 R§13
- **W-15 · An agent that can run code is tempted to fill rows from the text layer with a script.**
  → Every value is read from a page image; the text layer only cross-checks digits; a blind second reading is compared by the gate before any merge → CI§2.2, PHY-07 R§6-R§8
- **W-16 · A long session compacts and loses rules held only in conversation.**
  → Rules live in CLAUDE.md (re-read after compaction); state lives on disk (PROGRESS, part files, pushed packs) → CLAUDE.md §9

### I · Batch 2 (1 October, first Claude Code session)
- **B2-1 · The setup gave the scheme repository no role.** The vault file sits in the instructions repository and the 2026 schemes in a repository with neither a vault file nor a ZIP, so `phy_code_env.py` linked none of the scheme PDFs and inventory would have missed every one. Caught at boot from the setup's role lines; the PDFs were linked into /mnt/project by hand (links only) before inventory ran as CLAUDE.md §6 writes it.
  → At boot, every repository found must have a role or be opened by hand before inventory; Q-011 → CLAUDE.md §6, R§2
- **B2-2 · R§3's `render <file_id>` stopped with "cannot find document"** because the kit's `--vault` defaults to empty. Nothing was written from it.
  → Pass `--vault /home/claude/vault` to `pages` and `render`; Q-011 → R§3
- **B2-3 · Batch 1 misread the polarity of one cell in 55/3/1 Q17(a)** (F-2026-5531-02 puts E_2's longer plates towards B; the page shows them towards C, so the cells oppose and EQ-2026-5531-003's E_1 + E_2 is wrong). Every number on the row was right, so neither check-paper nor a numbers-only double-read could see it; the B02 extractor found it by comparing the sibling figures on 600-dpi crops, and both B02 rows describe the page.
  → A figure whose meaning depends on polarity or direction (cells, diodes, arrows, field lines) gets a crop on which plate lengths or arrowheads are measured, and its FIGURES description names the orientation; the stored rows are corrected through ERRATA (Q-013) -> CI s2.2, P s6.4
- **B2-4 · The 55/B/7 extractor wrote note text into the options column of 36 non-MCQ rows** (2026C-55B7-Q19 to -Q33B-ii); the gate check passed it and only the blind double-read showed it.
  → options is filled only when q_type is MCQ or AR; the double-read stays on every paper → R§5, R§8

# Y2026 — Claude's observations (judged text; every point backed by instance ids)

## SQP 2025-26 (SQP2526-042) — mined at Batch 0, 2026-09-29
- **Prediction step (S6).** First paper in the vault: no archetype statistics existed, so nothing could be predicted. All 34 codes it needed beyond the seeds were issued new; 19 seed archetypes were promoted by it.
- **Shape.** Blueprint class P33 exactly as the page-1 instructions print it: choice at Q20, Q21 (B), Q27 (C), Q31-Q33 (E); no choice in D. Section E splits: 2+2+1 (Q31(I), Q33(I)), 3+1+1 (Q31(II)), 3+2 (Q32(I), Q33(II)), 1+3+1 (Q32(II)).
- **Case formats differ inside one paper.** Q29 = four 1-mark MCQ sub-parts on diode circuits (SQP2526-042-Q29-I ... -IV); Q30 = three sub-parts worth 2+1+1 (numerical, prediction, graph: -Q30-I, -II, -III).
